opcodes.name: READ
opcodes.purpose: Clause 22 read of register REGAD in PHY PHYAD

opcodes.name: WRITE
opcodes.purpose: Clause 22 write of register REGAD in PHY PHYAD

opcodes.name: ADDRESS
opcodes.purpose: Load the 16-bit register address into the addressed MMD

opcodes.name: WRITE
opcodes.purpose: Write the previously addressed MMD register

opcodes.name: READ
opcodes.purpose: Read the previously addressed MMD register

opcodes.name: READ_INC
opcodes.purpose: Read then post-increment the register address

protocol_type: Fixed 32-bit management frame (after 32-bit preamble); STA-driven command portion, turnaround, PHY/STA data portion. Clause 22 direct register access; Clause 45 indirect addressing.

channels.name: MOSI
channels.description: Serial data: master drives data out / slave receives data in.

channels.name: MISO
channels.description: Serial data: slave drives data out / master receives data in.

channels.name: SCK
channels.description: Serial clock; master drives, slave samples.

channels.name: SS
channels.direction: master output (with SSOE) or input (mode-fault) / slave input

byte_order: Configurable MSB-first or LSB-first per LSBFE
single_response_for_write: No separate response channel; the same shift register cycle exchanges TX and RX data simultaneously.
per_beat_response_for_read: No; data on MISO is the slave's shift-out concurrent with master's MOSI shift-out.
valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no VALID/READY style handshake; SPI uses a free-running shift clock and a discrete SS slave-select.
Master drives 16 SCK edges to complete an 8-bit transfer (8 sample + 8 shift edges).
Slave aligns to master SCK and samples on the polarity+phase-defined edge.

access_types.SPIDR: Read / Write (read normally only when SPIF set; write anytime)

transaction_framing.start_S: HIGH-to-LOW transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.stop_P: LOW-to-HIGH transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.repeated_start_Sr: Functionally identical to S; keeps bus busy without an intervening STOP
transaction_framing.byte: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock pulse = 9 SCL cycles
transaction_framing.ack_bit: Receiver pulls SDA LOW during 9th SCL clock pulse
transaction_framing.nack_bit: SDA remains HIGH during 9th SCL clock pulse

address_byte_format.bits_0_to_7: 7-bit slave address (LSB-first into ADDRESS field, MSB-first on wire)
address_byte_format.bit_8: R/W direction bit; 0 = write to slave; 1 = read from slave
address_byte_format.10_bit_addressing: Two address bytes: first byte 0b11110XX0/1 (XX = upper 2 address bits + R/W); second byte = lower 8 address bits

rows: Reserved for future purposes including Device ID

master_to_slave_write_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=0 → ACK → DATA0 → ACK → DATA1 → ACK → … → P
Optional repeated START between bytes: S … DATA → ACK → Sr → SLAVE_ADDR2 || R/W → …
slave_to_master_read_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=1 → ACK (slave) → DATA0 (slave drives SDA) → ACK (master) → DATA1 → ACK → … → DATAN → NACK (master) → P

instructions_mandatory.name: BYPASS
instructions_mandatory.description: Connects TDI to TDO through the 1-bit Bypass register, adding only one TCK delay to the daisy chain. Used to shorten the chain when only some devices are being tested.

instructions_mandatory.name: SAMPLE/PRELOAD
instructions_mandatory.description: SAMPLE: in CaptureDR, the input BSCs capture the current value on their associated input pins and the output BSCs capture the value being driven on their output pins — a snapshot of pin activity during normal device operation. PRELOAD: in UpdateDR, the BSR contents are latched into the parallel-hold cells of the BSR so that EXTEST can begin driving the pre-loaded values without first-cycle indeterminate output.

instructions_mandatory.name: EXTEST
instructions_mandatory.description: External test. Output BSCs drive their associated output pins from the BSR-shifted values; input BSCs observe the values at their associated input pins (which therefore reflect the board-level interconnect or upstream device's output). Used for board-etch / solder-joint / interconnect testing.

instructions_optional.name: INTEST
instructions_optional.description: Internal test. The BSR drives the device's internal logic with shifted-in stimulus (BSR acts like a slow ATE pin set on the input side) and captures the internal-logic response on the output BSCs. Allows in-system functional testing of an IC's core logic.

instructions_optional.name: RUNBIST
instructions_optional.description: Run Built-In Self-Test. The TAP controller transitions into RunTestIdle, which the device interprets as 'run the BIST'. The BIST completion / result is read back via the selected register.

instructions_optional.name: CLAMP
instructions_optional.description: Drives the output pins from the pre-loaded BSR contents (set up via SAMPLE/PRELOAD) while the bypass register sits between TDI and TDO. Used to hold output values constant while a long bypass-only shift happens.

instructions_optional.name: HIGHZ
instructions_optional.description: Places all output pins in the high-impedance state. Useful for board-level fault isolation — disable the device's outputs to remove driver-conflict suspects.

instructions_optional.name: IDCODE
instructions_optional.description: Selects the 32-bit Device Identification register for shifting on TDO. The register contains version[31:28] / part-number[27:12] / manufacturer-id[11:1] / 1[0]. When a Device ID register is implemented, IDCODE is the post-reset default instruction.

instructions_optional.name: USERCODE
instructions_optional.description: Selects the Device ID register but loads it with a user-programmable 32-bit user code (e.g. FPGA configuration version, customer revision).

post_reset_default_instruction: IDCODE if a Device Identification Register is implemented; otherwise BYPASS.

data_register_catalog.name: Bypass
data_register_catalog.purpose: Single-bit TDI→TDO short-cut for BYPASS / CLAMP / HIGHZ instructions.

data_register_catalog.name: Boundary-Scan Register
data_register_catalog.purpose: Observation + drive of every device boundary pin for SAMPLE/PRELOAD / EXTEST / INTEST.

data_register_catalog.name: User-defined Data Register(s)
data_register_catalog.purpose: Vendor-specific test / debug / programming registers (e.g. SRAM scan, configuration shift, internal scan).

frame_format.ir_scan_sequence: TLR or RTI → SelectDRScan → SelectIRScan → CaptureIR → ShiftIR (N bits LSB-first) → Exit1IR → UpdateIR → RTI/SelectDRScan.
frame_format.dr_scan_sequence: RTI or TLR → SelectDRScan → CaptureDR → ShiftDR (M bits LSB-first) → Exit1DR → UpdateDR → RTI/SelectDRScan.
frame_format.bit_order: LSB first into ShiftIR / ShiftDR; the first bit shifted in is the LSB of the destination register; the first bit shifted out on TDO is the LSB of the captured register.
frame_format.interleaved_chain: In a daisy chain, the shift register seen by the tester is the concatenation of (in order) each device's selected register; bypass-set devices contribute 1 bit each.

mdio_clause22_frame.PRE: 32 contiguous logic-1 bits on MDIO with 32 corresponding MDC cycles. May be suppressed if both ends support preamble suppression (BMSR bit 1.6).
mdio_clause22_frame.ST: <01> — start of frame, ensures transitions from default-1 line state.
mdio_clause22_frame.PHYAD: 5 bits, MSB first. 32 unique addresses; PHYAD 00000 always responded to by a single-PHY connection.
mdio_clause22_frame.REGAD: 5 bits, MSB first. 32 registers; register 0 = BMCR, register 1 = BMSR, register 2/3 = PHY ID, register 4 = ANAR, register 5 = ANLPAR, register 6 = ANER, register 9 = 1000BASE-T Control, register 10 = 1000BASE-T Status, register 15 = Extended Status.
mdio_clause22_frame.TA: 2 bits. Read: bit-0 = high-impedance (both sides), bit-1 = 0 driven by PHY. Write: <10> driven by STA.
mdio_clause22_frame.DATA: 16 bits. First bit on the wire = bit 15 of the register being accessed.

mdio_clause45_frame.OP: <00> = Address (write 16-bit register address into the MMD), <01> = Write data, <11> = Read data, <10> = Post-Increment Read.
mdio_clause45_frame.DEVAD: 5-bit MMD Device Address. Defined MMDs: 1 PMA/PMD, 2 WIS, 3 PCS, 4 PHY XS, 5 DTE XS, 6 TC, 7 Auto-Negotiation, 13/14 EEE, 29 Clause 22 register access, 30/31 Vendor-specific.
mdio_clause45_frame.DATA: Address cycle: 16-bit register address. Data cycle: 16-bit register value (the previously written address selects the register).

addressing: 5-bit PHYAD/PRTAD selects PHY/port (in-frame), not a separate chip-select wire or an I2C slave-address+ACK

frame_fields.desc: Turnaround: 10 on write, Z0 on read

turnaround.read: Z0 (STA tri-states bit 1, PHY drives 0 in bit 2)

indirect_addressing: Clause 45 only: Address frame (OP=00) loads a 16-bit register address; subsequent Write/Read/Read-Increment frames operate on it
